headline: Neural models encode regulatory and transcriptomic structure beyond linear methods
label: Deep Learning Regulatory Genomics
summary: Recent preprints and papers pair deep architectures with prior biological knowledge, spanning pathway enrichment to perturbation prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is neural architectures applied to omics and sequencing data, where model structure is tied to biological organization. LaCoGSEA uses an autoencoder with gene-latent correlation rankings for unsupervised pathway enrichment, and TwinPurify adapts Barlow Twins to purify bulk tumor transcriptomes using adjacent-normal profiles as background. Several items add explicit prior knowledge: MapPFN is pre-trained on synthetic causal biological priors for in-context perturbation prediction, PIMO uses pathway-based interpretable multi-omics interactions, and KGBN augments logical gene regulatory networks with knowledge-graph-derived rules. Interpretability and benchmarking appear alongside these methods: scGeneLens dissects single-cell foundation models with integrated gradients, while a structural variant filtering benchmark finds a simple Random Forest matches ResNet and diffusion models. The set is heterogeneous, and the shared link is architectural rather than a common task.
